A1.justification: Despite the changed title and substantial reframing, both PDFs share the authors and the CLIP/SigLIP Information Gain and covariance-weighted embedding framework. All 11 pages of v1 and 27 pages of v2 are readable, including equations, visual results, and v2's supplementary Sections 8–12. v1 has no appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original CC12M and Visual Genome analyses, experiments training normalized and unnormalized SigLIP models, and correlations between Information Gain and embedding metrics.

after.justification: v2 reports original importance-weighted training curves, MSCOCO analyses, and KL-based data-curation results, including supplementary SigLIP experiments. Table 1 explicitly distinguishes cited DataComp baseline scores from the proposed methods' results.

M1.justification: v1 estimates batch posteriors and an averaged marginal, then approximates Information Gain with covariance-weighted norms. v2 reformulates estimation through scaled density ratios, introduces reverse KL and a centered Euclidean-norm variant, and adds two substantive procedures: prompt-weighted CLIP training through Eq. (7) and KL-based top-quartile data selection in Section 5.3. The covariance approximation idea remains.

E1.justification: CC12M remains training data, but its earlier informativeness analyses and the Visual Genome attribute evaluation are replaced by MSCOCO caption analyses. v2 adds domain-specific downstream evaluations on Food101, Oxford-IIIT Pet and Flowers102, plus DataComp-small curation evaluated across 38 classification and retrieval tasks, including ImageNet1k.

E2.justification: v1's comparisons focus on raw norms, covariance-weighted norms and caption/attribute proxies. v2 adds unweighted CLIP training as the IWL control in Figures 2 and 12, and compares curation against no filtering, LAION2B, Basic and CLIPScore in Table 1. Those table baseline scores are explicitly reused from DataComp rather than established as new runs.

E3.justification: v1's 32-epoch SigLIP normalization experiments and R2-based evaluation are not retained. New v2 protocols include ten-epoch ViT-B/32 training, a CLIP ViT-L/14 weighting reference with logit scale 10, and accuracy/F1 learning curves. DataComp experiments retain 25% of the pool and use 10,000 reference images and texts. These are different experiments, not same-setting performance comparisons.

E4.justification: v1's training/inference normalization ablations, direct norm-versus-KL validation, and correlations with caption length, LLaMA probability and annotated attributes disappear, including from the supplement. v2 introduces N-gram coverage analyses by KL decile and extensive image/text case studies comparing forward KL, reverse KL and norm variants across CLIP and SigLIP (Sections 5.2 and 11–12).

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run aggregates, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v1's R2 values measure association; v2's discussion of finite-sample bias and variance does not introduce an uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v1's correlation results, including normalized SigLIP covariance-norm R2 values of 0.98 for images and 0.96 for text in Table 3, are removed. v2 adds IWL curves, N-gram findings and filtering results. Its Table 1 reports text forward-KL ImageNet accuracy/mean metrics of 0.0300/0.1337, versus LAION2B's 0.031/0.133 and CLIPScore's 0.051/0.173. These results have no corresponding v1 benchmark setting.

T1.justification: v2 retains a revised covariance approximation but adds explicit density-ratio formulations for CLIP and SigLIP, covariate-shift assumptions and importance-weighting identities, reverse-KL definitions, and supplementary derivations. v1's memory-complexity argument is removed. The new forward-KL expressions in Eqs. (10) and (34) contain an extra similarity factor inside the logarithmic normalizer, inconsistent with Eq. (33).

C1.justification: The central contribution changes from semantic informativeness and efficient covariance-norm approximation to CLIP-like models as general-purpose density-ratio estimators. v2's abstract, introduction and conclusion foreground prompt-driven importance weighting, semantic diversity and competitive LAION2B-style filtering. v1's headline claims about near-perfect norm correlations and memory efficiency no longer define the contribution.

C2.justification: v1 emphasizes embedding normalization and possible explanations for high-scoring illustrations. v2 develops interpretations involving contextual diversity, prompt-based soft weighting, and KL filtering as complementary to alignment, explicitly acknowledging that it does not surpass CLIPScore. Limitations now discuss transfer from pretraining distributions, model bias, temperature and sampling effects, and restricted experimental scale and domains.

D1.justification: Compared with v1's sparse training details, v2 Section 10 documents AdamW, learning rate 5e-4, weight decay 0.2, mixed precision, eight GPUs, global batch size 8000, data-loader workers and approximately 70 H200 GPU-hours per model. It also identifies the OpenCLIP pipeline and explains the weighting-scale reduction to avoid overflow. The abstract promises future code availability; it does not establish a release.

R1.justification: Related work shifts substantially from word norms, keyword extraction and distributional semantics toward density-ratio estimation, covariate-shift adaptation and data curation. v2 adds discussion of KLIEP, uLSIF, logistic density-ratio estimation, InfoNCE and CLIPScore while retaining the relevant Oyama, CLIP, SigLIP and DataComp connections. Its novelty positioning broadens to general-purpose multimodal density-ratio applications.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work and conclusion are extensively rewritten. v1's two research questions and informativeness/norm-centered organization become a density-ratio foundation followed by application sections and four contribution statements. A substantial supplement organizes derivations, training details and additional analyses. This is a broad narrative restructuring, beyond simply inserting experiments.

P2.justification: The single-column presentation becomes a two-column layout with wide figures and supplementary displays. v1's correlation scatterplot tables and complexity table disappear. v2 introduces learning-curve panels, N-gram plots, large ranked image/caption grids and a data-curation results table. The earlier compact examples are replaced with different examples and substantially redesigned displays.

improvement.justification: v2 adds practical downstream validation absent from v1, broader derivations and substantially better training documentation. However, it removes direct approximation-validation experiments and introduces a central inconsistency between the forward-KL estimator in Eqs. (10)/(34) and Eq. (33). Section 5.3 also claims 5–8 percentage-point gains where Table 1 shows only 0.5–0.75 points over no filtering. The PDFs do not establish whether the formula errors are typographical or affected computation. These unresolved correctness and reporting issues prevent a reliable net-quality judgment despite the useful additions.
